items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Paginate every endpoint used by the watcher**

When a PR has more than one page of commits, reviews, or review comments, these bare `gh api` calls inspect only the first page and can miss the later P0/P1 item that crosses the stop threshold. `gh api --help` states that `--paginate` “fetch[es] all pages of results,” and Worker Playbook step 15 already documents that the review and comment endpoints return 30 items per page. Add `--paginate` to each list call (or require the paginating counter for every applicable count) so the promised watch of every in-flight task is complete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include every review finding in the S1 class count**

When the repeated class appears in P2/P3 review-body findings, or is distributed across Codex and another reviewer, this procedure never reaches three because it selects only P0/P1 Codex review bodies and otherwise only Codex comments. That conflicts with the existing S1 invariant in this file, which counts the same class three times “from any reviewer” and assigns a class to every PR-feedback finding regardless of disposition, so the worker can continue instead of stopping after S1 has actually fired.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:the worker-side count is the early stop over the Codex Bot's badged findings by design; S1 is the orchestrator's ledger over every sweep item

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Encode review-derived classes before dispatching the PONG**

When a Bot title echoes shell syntax from the reviewed diff, the prescribed class is raw review-derived text whose only normalization is lower-casing, yet Worker step 11 sends PONGs through `agmsg-dispatch` as a positional shell argument. For example, a first-three-word class containing `$(...)` can be expanded by the caller's shell before dispatch; step 6 explicitly warns that this exact positional path executes and removes command substitutions. Encode the class and thread values into a shell-safe alphabet or send the body through a file-capable path, and add the missing control for this PR-controlled-input boundary to the threat table.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/9d001bcb336f256a999186f052807e4cfcc84bca/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Choose one third-round handoff instead of waiting forever**

On the third Bot round with inline P0/P1 findings, the two post-RESULT fix heads make this new rule reach `heads=2`, so it requires a blocked PONG followed by waiting for an ACCEPTANCE. The immediately following rule still requires that same third round to send `AGMSG-RESULT … bot_rounds=3`, and the contract at line 131 plus Orchestrator step 8 use that RESULT to start disposition and acceptance. A worker following the new instruction therefore waits before sending the message that enables its release; define a single handoff for this overlapping INV-6/A2 case.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the complete counter output in validation**

Every `--history-only` invocation emits both the count line and a `detail:` line, with one or more `S2:` lines when a threshold fires, but this instruction tells the worker to paste only the count line. That contradicts the RESULT evidence rule at line 121 requiring verbatim output from every validation command and also drops the very S2 evidence referenced later in this sentence, so an otherwise compliant RESULT can be rejected as incomplete. Require the complete command output to be pasted.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Quarantine a forced worker worktree before reseating it**

When the stopped worker has uncommitted edits, `--force` merely bypasses `herdr-agents`' dirty-worktree refusal; it does not clean or remove the worktree, and `--add-worker` has no cleanliness check. Re-creating a seat there for the next task can therefore make its fresh branch fail to check out or carry the abandoned task's edits into unrelated work. Require cleanup after preserving evidence, or seat the next task in a separate clean worktree instead.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L27-L29](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/9d001bcb336f256a999186f052807e4cfcc84bca/AGENTS.md#L27-L29)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count non-review feedback toward S1**

When the same class occurs three times in check-run annotations, non-passing checks, statuses, or issue comments, this procedure cannot count it because it fetches only reviews, review comments, and commits, then further describes the inputs as “inline or review-body.” However, `scripts/pr-feedback.py:181-264` emits all of those additional sources, and the existing S1 invariant requires a class for every finding that sweep lists. The fresh evidence since the earlier comment is this revised source list: despite adding “any reviewer, any priority,” it still omits non-review sweep items, so the worker can continue after S1 has fired.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ping workers as soon as a stop threshold is crossed**

When a runaway worker keeps pushing less than 45 minutes apart, those pushes continually prevent the only stated condition that sends a PING (“45 minutes without a push”), while forced removal requires that a PING already exist and remain unread. Consequently, even though the watch observes the worker crossing the A2 or INV-6 cap, it has no prescribed transition that sends the stop PING, so an active worker that ignores its self-stop can continue indefinitely. Send the PING when the watch first observes either threshold, then apply the unread/continued-pushing removal rule.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:

When a PR receives three ordinary comments with the same opening—such as repeated `@codex review` requests or review replies—this rule reaches S1 even though no finding was repeated, because `scripts/pr-feedback.py:181-215` emits every issue comment, review, and inline reply without a finding predicate. The fresh evidence since the earlier source-coverage comment is the revised `one per item` wording, which turns those untrusted non-finding items into stop signals; require a finding predicate and cover that semantic trust boundary in the threat table.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/040b32f9cfd88eb311f985a16ff434d6591acfbf/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accumulate head-scoped feedback across fix rounds**

When the same failing check, annotation, or commit status recurs once on each of three successive heads, no single `scripts/pr-feedback.py <pr>` result contains all three occurrences: `collect()` binds check runs and statuses to the current `pull["head"]["sha"]` at `scripts/pr-feedback.py:176-219`. The fresh evidence after the earlier non-review-source finding is that the replacement now names this current-head sweep without preserving prior-head results, so the repeated class remains at one and S1 never fires; retain and combine each round's sweep or query those sources for every task head.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define the S1-only third-round handoff**

When the third Bot round raises the third instance of a P2/P3 or review-body class but `heads` remains below 2, this paragraph requires a blocked PONG while step 15 still unconditionally requires a `bot_rounds=3` RESULT. The fresh evidence after the prior handoff finding is that the new exception is explicitly limited to `heads=2`; extend the one-handoff rule to an S1-only stop so the worker has one executable instruction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop workers that read but ignore the threshold PING**

When delivery marks the threshold PING read but the worker ignores its content and continues pushing, the only forced-removal rule no longer applies because it requires the PING to stay unread. Such an active noncompliant worker can therefore keep producing heads past A2 or INV-6 indefinitely; make continued pushing without the required stop response sufficient for removal, regardless of `read_at`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude predecessor feedback from reset successors**

When an S1 reset successor continues on the same PR, the predecessor's three triggering findings remain among the items returned by `scripts/pr-feedback.py`, so the successor immediately reaches S1 again despite this sentence promising that it inherits no classes. In particular, issue comments have no commit boundary and `scripts/pr-feedback.py:203-215` omits `original_commit_id` from review-comment items, making the stated first-commit filter impossible for non-Codex and issue-comment findings; introduce task-span metadata/filtering and a corresponding cross-task-isolation control in the threat table.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/040b32f9cfd88eb311f985a16ff434d6591acfbf/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate arbitrary feedback text before the worker reads it**

When a non-Codex reviewer, issue commenter, check annotation, or status supplies instruction-like text, the new all-source class count causes the worker to run `scripts/pr-feedback.py <pr>`, whose default output contains each complete untrusted body, and interpret that output before sanitization. This threat-table row only reduces the derived class for later shell transport and therefore does not mitigate model-level prompt injection from the newly included sources; use a deterministic extractor that exposes only normalized class and identifier fields, and add the missing trust-boundary control.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/040b32f9cfd88eb311f985a16ff434d6591acfbf/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add a control for forced worker removal**

When GitHub/history state is stale or associated with the wrong task, this new procedure can execute `herdr-agents --remove-worker <worktree> --force` against an active seat, but the task's threat table covers only the edited artifacts and review text placed in messages; it has no row controlling the task-to-PR/worktree binding, threshold revalidation, or this forced in-process effect. Add a threat-table row with a concrete verification or compensating control before permitting removal.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/3ba70625d75cb8b5816406aacaa76d00d41a2525/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Paginate the worker's review and commit lookups**

When a PR has more than one page of reviews or commits, this worker instruction explicitly applies `--paginate` only to the comments lookup, so the abbreviated reviews and commits calls can omit the task's first commit or later review-body findings and produce incorrect stop counts. `gh api --help` confirms that `--paginate` is what makes the CLI request additional pages. The fresh evidence after the earlier pagination comment is that step 7 now explicitly says all three calls paginate, while this worker-side instruction still does not; specify `gh api --paginate` for reviews and commits here as well.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include lower-priority review bodies in class counting**

When the repeated class occurs in three P2/P3 review-body findings, the worker never reaches the promised early stop because the input list still selects only review bodies carrying P0/P1 badges. The fresh evidence after the earlier finding is the final sentence added on this head that now explicitly claims review bodies of “any priority” are counted, directly contradicting that P0/P1 filter; list all badged P0–P3 review bodies for class counting while retaining the narrower fix-cap and INV-6 rules.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the first RESULT to carry its head**

When a worker sends a contract-valid first RESULT without a `head=` field, this procedure has no baseline from which to count later P0/P1 heads, so INV-6 can remain unknown and the worker will not self-stop. The Message Contract currently requires only task/status and artifact fields for RESULT, while `scripts/regime-counters.sh` likewise returns an unknown Bot-head count when the first RESULT lacks `head=`; make `head=<sha>` mandatory before relying on “its first RESULT's head.”

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Watch the audit-head component of INV-6**

When P0/P1 implementation or specification audit findings recur on two post-RESULT heads, INV-6 is reached by the design invariant, but this watch reads only GitHub commits, reviews, comments, checks, and PONG history. `scripts/regime-counters.sh` currently prints `audits=unknown` and does not read the task audit files or their `AGMSG-AUDIT` records, so neither the threshold PING nor forced stop occurs for this INV-6 component; include the authenticated audit-head source (or explicitly defer this component to its owning phase) before claiming to react to any INV-6 count.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the audit artifact format that currently exists**

When two P0/P1 audit findings occur on successive revision heads before the planned V2 audit runner lands, this watch cannot observe them: the current task-level audit procedure at lines 80–85 creates only `<task>-audit-<sha7>.md` and `.last.md`, does not create the referenced JSON, and does not emit an `AGMSG-AUDIT` hash record. Fresh evidence after the earlier audit-head comment is that this commit added the JSON lookup without adding a V2 dependency or a fallback for the current artifacts, so the worker can continue past the audit component of INV-6. Use the current authenticated audit source until V2 is available, and cover the artifact-to-record binding in the task's threat table.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Establish the PR identifier before starting the watch**

For a newly dispatched task, the worker creates the draft PR after receiving `AGMSG-TASK`, but that message contract has no PR field and the worker sends no milestone message after `gh pr create`; the first required handoff can remain the final RESULT. Consequently, during the in-flight period when the worker can exceed the A2 cap, the orchestrator has no `<n>` for any of these GitHub calls, so the promised threshold PING and forced stop cannot run. Require the worker to report the PR number immediately after creation, or prescribe a reliable lookup from task metadata before beginning the watch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count repeated findings even when no fix commit follows**

The class scan is required only “before each fix commit,” so it is skipped when a round has only P2/P3 findings that the worker proposes to disposition, and necessarily on the third Bot round because the following rule forbids fixing that round. If either case supplies the third occurrence of a class, the worker never observes the S1 stop despite the later third-round handoff clause. Run the class scan after every Bot review round, before deciding whether a fix commit will be made.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define how the watcher derives the A2 fix-round count**

The new removal path depends on the orchestrator detecting that a task is past the A2 cap, but none of the prescribed reads yields a fix-round count: `scripts/regime-counters.sh` reports revision, amendment, question, and post-RESULT Bot-head counts, while an arbitrary commit list does not identify which commits are Bot-finding fixes. This is especially important before the first RESULT, when the INV-6 Bot-head counter has no baseline but the worker can already exceed its two fix rounds. Define a deterministic A2 counter or add an authenticated worker milestone so the PING/removal condition can actually be evaluated.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the first RESULT head to the observed PR head**

When a worker mistakenly reports an older commit from the same PR, making `head` mandatory does not ensure that it is the head that actually produced the first RESULT: `scripts/regime-counters.sh` accepts any 7–40-character prefix found in the PR commit list and then counts findings after that commit. This can include pre-RESULT findings and falsely trigger INV-6. Validate the field against the PR head observed when the first RESULT arrives, and add the corresponding input-binding control to this trust-boundary task's threat table.
